nar.text: The cars started individually in order of their race numbers at intervals of two minutes.
The morning sun forewarned a glowing hot day above the Madonie Mountains when at 7am the start was given to Dubonnet
Minoia starts as 16B, having been allowed to change his number 17.

At the end of the first lap, no less than six drivers remained below Masetti's existing lap record.
For the first time at the Targa Florio none of the drivers retired during the first lap, something that had never happened before.
Masetti was in the lead with an average speed of 67.406 km/h

Due to the hot weather and the numerous sharp exposed stones on the course, many drivers had to stop already at the beginning of the second lap to change tires which transformed the order in the field.
Werner laps in 1h34m59.8s and takes the lead after 3h11m45s.
Ascari made up some time and was two minutes behind Werner while Boilot was now third and Masetti dropped to fourth place.
Dubonnet had to change two tires and re-joined in 11th position.
Mucera and Philipp retire out on the course.

On the third lap Werner remained in the lead, followed by Ascari who now was nearly three minutes behind the leader.
Boillot dropped to fourth place after he made an excursion into a bean field resulting with tire damage.
Boillot was in despair about the long wait of nearly nine minutes before he rejoined.
Seven cars retired on the third lap, reducing the field to 28 cars. Caruso slowly passed the grandstands with his defective Bianchi to retire

At the beginning of the fourth lap, Werner had to stop at the depot to change tires, likewise other front runners like Rützler, Foresti, Bordiono and Masetti.
The time difference between Werner and Ascari was now just a few seconds and Werner's stop had been accurately signaled to Ascari, who in turn saw his chance to win.
When the roaring car took the last uphill turn only 30 meters before the finish, it abruptly became silent and spun around. The engine had seized solid causing the forceful stop.
Officials intervened, explaining to the helpers after an intense battle of words that with their rashness they had prevented Ascari to finish. Outside assistance was not allowed.
Kaufmann crashes his Steiger in a turn and retires unhurt.
Minoia (Steyr) retired on the course when his mechanic Hansal suffered a heat stroke and needed medical help.
Werner (Mercedes) finished first over eight minutes ahead of Masetti (Alfa Romeo) and Bordini (Fiat) was third.
